title: Streamlined Token Flux dashboard — compact + expanded model & route inspector
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Background: PMs and SREs need a single inspector that surfaces token-level cost, latency distribution, and throughput behavior for both model variants and per-route usage. Existing canvases are either too wide (detail) or too abstract (single sparklines) — teams ask for a compact summary row they can expand into a microtrace view without leaving the route/model context.

Scope: Design a dual-mode UI tile (Compact & Expanded) named 'Token Flux' that fits in the Route Overview grid and expands into an inline overlay panel. The tile must show: median+P95 latency ribbon, tokens/sec throughput sparkline (with rolling window), token-cost slope (cost/token heatmap), KV-cache hit overlay, and per-variant micro-sparklines. Expanded view includes swimlane microtraces for slow requests, a ridgeline of latency distribution slices, and a token-waterfall event list for diagnostic drilling.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-diagnose from Route Overview to root cause by 40% for token-related regressions.
- Keep compact tile height <= 96px and usable on 3-up dashboard grid.
- Ensure colorblind-safe palette and keyboard navigability for expanded views.

Out of scope: full rollout controls (handled in separate rollout ticket) and long-term retention UI (handled by telemetry retention project).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Compact tile implemented as prototype with clear legend that fits 3-up grid and contains median/P95 ribbon, throughput sparkline, and cost heat cell.
2) Expanded inline overlay prototype includes latency ridgeline, microtrace swimlane, and token waterfall list.
3) Hover interactions: hover over sparkline shows token/sec snapshot and KV-cache hit %.
4) Keyboard users can focus tile and open overlay with Enter; screen readers announce summary metrics.
5) Dev-ready chart specs (SVG + canvas fallback) documented and linked.
6) Design reviewed and approved by Eng + PM; review comments triaged.
decisions:
- Use compact height of 96px to balance density and legibility.
- Use a combined SVG ridgeline for latency distribution instead of stacked histograms to reduce visual noise in expanded view.
- Encode KV-cache hit as a thin overlay band on throughput sparkline to reduce vertical real estate.
- Prefer colorblind-safe diverging palette (blue → orange) with texture hatch in waterfall rows for high-contrast printing.
- Use canvas renderer for throughput sparkline at >3000 points, SVG for other charts for crispness and accessibility semantics.
tradeoffs:
- Chose ridgeline over stacked histograms: simpler to read distributions but loses exact per-bin counts. Team agreed counts can be surfaced on hover to mitigate.
- Compact tile sacrifices single-request trace detail; expanded overlay restores that context but requires one extra interaction.
- Using canvas for high-density traces improves perf but reduces native DOM semantics; implemented aria-sync to expose synthetic descriptors for screen readers.
review_feedback: PM feedback (Samir Patel): emphasize cost-per-token callouts for top-10 routes; add callout variance baseline.
Eng feedback (Evan Brooks): prefer canvas for throughput at scale; request clear perf budget and fallback behavior. Added ticket ENG-2045 for infra changes.
Accessibility review (Priya Kapoor): add keyboard flow + description nodes; ensure high-contrast mode handles ridgeline textures.
mockup_versions: v0.1-wireframe (Feb 12) - initial layout and metric set
v0.2-visual (Feb 20) - color palette, compact ribbon, heat-cell
next_steps:
1) Finalize chart props document and hand off to ENG (ENG-2045) with perf budgets.
2) Build interactive prototype for user testing (3 sessions with internal SREs).
3) Update Console design system tokens for new heat-cell component.
4) Coordinate with PM to add top-10 route cost callout in route brief.
5) Track engineering implementation in linked PR and iterate on micro-interactions.
